title: Point transport on whole coefficient systems, powers and integral realization
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. On the small pro-etale site of $s$, set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_n B_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the abelian category $\mathscr S_s$ of strict semilinear $B_n$-module systems and its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers, $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$, and $\mathcal R_sN$ for the simultaneous derived reduction system [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $G_r$ be exact termwise inverse image along $h^r$, using the canonical coefficient isomorphisms. Its levels are identified with the termwise module pullbacks $(h^r)^*M_n=(h^r)^{-1}M_n\otimes_{(h^r)^{-1}B_n}B_n$ by the isomorphisms $j_r:x\mapsto x\otimes1$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (a); every map below is read through this identification, so that the finite point transports land in $\Gamma(s,L(h^r)^*C_n)$. Let $t_m:G_1G_m\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{m+1}$ be the canonical inverse-image compositor, in the direction inverse to [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Define $\Gamma_\bullet C$ by applying restriction of scalars and $\Gamma(s,-)$ to each level of a complex of systems; it is a functor $D(\mathscr S_s)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}R))$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For EVERY $C\in D(\mathscr S_s)$, not necessarily a reduction system of an integral input, restriction along $h^r$, insertion into the inverse-image colimit and sheafification, and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ at each level, in the recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], define a specified natural tower map
$$I_{r,C}:\Gamma_\bullet C\longrightarrow\Gamma_\bullet G_rC.$$
The recipe is applied to complexes of whole semilinear systems before localization; its transition maps are the given semilinear transitions of $C$. If the evaluations $C_n$ are bounded constructible, the evaluation of $I_{r,C}$ is exactly the finite point transport $\iota^{(r)}_{C_n}$. For every derived SYSTEM morphism $u:C\to D$, and every $m\geq1$, the following are identities in the derived category of whole $R$-module towers:
$$\Gamma_\bullet(G_ru)\circ I_{r,C}=I_{r,D}\circ\Gamma_\bullet(u),$$
$$I_{m+1,C}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,C})\circ I_{1,G_mC}\circ I_{m,C}.$$

Here is the realization normalization, including its actual comparison maps. Put $N=\mathcal L_sC$ and assume only $N\in D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $P_r=L(h^r)^*$ for completed integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let
$$\nu_{r,C}:P_rN\xrightarrow{\sim}(h^r)^{-1}N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC$$
use the coefficient isomorphism $ (h^r)^{-1}\widehat R_s\cong\widehat R_s$, the INVERSE of the specified integral map $\kappa_N:(h^r)^{-1}N\to P_rN$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b), and commutation of the exact inverse-image equivalence with the total derived limit [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. The assertion includes invertibility of this specified $\kappa_N$ on the stated derived-complete domain. The latter comparison is the derived map of the entire limit cone: on a tower resolution it is inverse image applied to its limit-cone map, not a choice of identifications of individual evaluations. Let $\zeta_C:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal L_sC)$ be the comparison induced by applying exact sections, which preserve products, to the total-limit model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then the actual maps satisfy
$$\zeta_{G_rC}\circ R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,\nu_{r,C})\circ\iota_N^{(r)}\circ\zeta_C.$$
All these comparisons are natural for system morphisms. They respect the compositors as follows. The object $P_mN$ lies in $D^b_c(s,R)$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], hence so does $\mathcal L_sG_mC\cong P_mN$, and $\nu_{1,G_mC}$ is defined. Let $c^E_{m,N}:P_{m+1}N\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1P_mN$ be the specified integral pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] for $h$ followed by $h^m$. Then
$$\nu_{m+1,C}=\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})\circ\nu_{1,G_mC}\circ P_1(\nu_{m,C})\circ c^E_{m,N}.$$
 In particular for $C=\mathcal R_sN$ this recovers the powerwise version of [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization]; the formula also applies directly to a finite-output compact-support system with bounded constructible derived limit. No finite Tor-amplitude, normalization, or reconstruction assumption on $C$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-point-system-power-roos-coherence] to obtain the stated power law with the specified $t_m$, and retain its identity $a_{m+1}d_m=\mathcal L_s(t_m)a_{1,G_mC}F_1(a_m)$ for the normalized whole-limit comparisons.

source.place: Assembly step 2; clause (3), whole-system integral transport

proof.text: By [lem-trf-point-system-roos-transport], the actual cone-normalized maps $a_r,\zeta$ are natural and satisfy $\zeta_{G_rC}R\lim(I_r)=\Gamma(s,a_r)\sigma_{r,N}\zeta_C$ for $N=\mathcal L_sC$, without assumptions on $C$ or $N$.

source.place: Assembly step 3; clause (3), whole-system integral transport

proof.text: Now suppose $N\in D^b_c(s,R)$. Its derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] makes the actual $\kappa^{(r)}_N$ invertible by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], naturally with the specified zero-shifted-coordinate completion augmentation. Put $\nu_r=a_r(\kappa^{(r)}_N)^{-1}$. The defining recipe [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] gives $\iota_N^{(r)}=\Gamma(s,\kappa^{(r)}_N)\sigma_{r,N}$. Cancellation in step 3 proves precisely the asserted realization identity and its naturality.

source.place: Assembly step 4; clause (3), whole-system integral transport

proof.text:
The object $P_mN$ is constructible by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]; hence so is $\mathcal L_sG_mC\cong P_mN$. With the specified $c^E$ of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], [lem-trf-integral-inverse-image-comparison-composition] gives $c^E_m\kappa^{(m+1)}_Nd_m=\kappa^{(1)}_{P_mN}F_1(\kappa^{(m)}_N)$. Naturality of $\kappa^{(1)}$ at $
u_m$, inversion of this equality, and step 2 yield
$$\mathcal L_s(t_m)
u_{1,G_mC}P_1(
u_m)c^E_m=\mathcal L_s(t_m)a_{1,G_mC}F_1(a_m)d_m^{-1}(\kappa^{(m+1)}_N)^{-1}=a_{m+1}(\kappa^{(m+1)}_N)^{-1}=
u_{m+1}.$$
This proves compositor compatibility for these actual whole-cone maps.

source.place: Assembly step 5; Global powers, compatibility with composition

proof.text: For $N_0\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and $C=\mathcal R_sN_0$, [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] supplies the simultaneous quotient system, and the $L=E$ completion isomorphism of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies its limit with $N_0$ by the actual quotient augmentation. Steps 1 and 4 give the reduction-tower specialization for every power. Any finite-output system with constructible limit satisfies step 4 directly. No reconstruction of $C$, normalization, or finite Tor-amplitude was used.
